unresolved_candidates.source_text: Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will repay your recompense upon your heads,
unresolved_candidates.reason: This actual passage combines difficult questions about giants and captors with rescue of sons and punishment of afflicters. The broad rescue-and-judgment theme was not retained as a counterpart to rousing people from where they were sold. The more particular recompense-upon-the-head formula in Obadiah 1:15 was retained instead.

target_units.text: Will anyone take spoils from a giant? If someone takes captives unjustly, will he be saved?”
Thus says the Lord: “If someone captures a giant, he will take spoils; one taking from a strong man will be saved. I will judge your case, and I will rescue your sons.
Those who afflicted you will eat their own flesh, drink their own blood like new wine, and become drunk. All flesh will perceive that I am the Lord who rescued you and upholds Jacob’s strength.”

unresolved_candidates.source_text: But Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generations upon generations.
unresolved_candidates.reason: This actual passage promises permanence for a city and sanctuary area, but these units do not expressly name Jerusalem and the final pronoun follows the described sacred area. Rather than resolve those names and pronouns for this comparison, the explicit promise of Jerusalem's habitation in Zechariah 14:11 was retained.

target_units.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and a city will be built for the Lord from Hanamel’s tower to the Corner Gate.
And its measurement will go out opposite them as far as Gareb’s hills, and it will be enclosed all around with chosen stones.
And all Asaremoth as far as the Kidron wadi, to the corner of the eastern Horse Gate, will be a sanctuary for the Lord. It will certainly never disappear or be torn down for ever.
